This release expands the skill from lean/over-engineering review to a full quality review including bugs, tests, security, scale, and performance.

- Broadens scope to review for bugs, security, scalability, missing tests, and slowness, while still flagging unnecessary code.
- Adds detailed review process: read diff, follow code flows, check real-world use and expected load.
- Outputs findings in clear groups (Must fix, Should fix, Nice to have), with concrete problems and fixes for each.
- Makes reporting style simple and actionable, with clear explanations and numbering across all findings.
- Updates boundaries: no style/taste issues, only real technical or operational problems.
- Removes previous card/summary file (skill-card.md); now SKILL.md gives full details.

- Removed the documentation file skill-card.md.

- Findings are now numbered for easier referencing and action, e.g., `1. L12-38: ...`
- Example output updated to illustrate the new numbering scheme.
- Formatting section updated to specify report-wide sequential numbering.

- Updated skill description for clarity: reviews diffs for over-engineering and highlights what to delete in concise, one-line findings.
- Standardized output format with tags for deletions, stdlib, native features, YAGNI issues, and line shrinking.
- Added clear, side-by-side examples contrasting verbose vs. concise findings.
- Defined boundaries: focus strictly on complexity and over-engineering, excluding correctness, security, and performance.
- Formalized scoring: report possible net line reduction, or "Lean already. Ship." if nothing to cut.
